combinations.name: Benzodiazepines
combinations.description: The classic fatal pairing — both suppress breathing by different mechanisms, and the combination is behind a large share of opioid deaths. Tolerance to one gives no protection against the other. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: Additive respiratory depression, and alcohol impairs the arousal response that would otherwise wake you when breathing slows. A moderate amount of either becomes dangerous together. Do not combine.

combinations.name: MAOIs
combinations.description: Opioid–MAOI interactions range from serotonin toxicity to unpredictable potentiation of sedation and blood pressure effects. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Gabapentinoids
combinations.description: Gabapentin and pregabalin add their own respiratory depression on top of the opioid's — a pairing increasingly represented in overdose data precisely because each half seems mild alone. If both are prescribed, keep doses conservative and avoid stacking extra sedatives.

combinations.name: Other opioids
combinations.description: Different names, one receptor — doses stack directly. Adding a second opioid on top of oxycodone is a dose increase, not a different drug; count the total.
